content: When using this medication, it is essential to be aware of potential drug interactions, as they can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of severe side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. It is recommended to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication should not be used in combination with certain drugs due to the risk of very serious interactions. Specifically, taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) with this medication can result in a severe, potentially fatal reaction. Avoid using MAOIs such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, metaxalone, methylene blue, moclobemide, phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, or tranylcypromine during treatment with this medication. Additionally, most MAOIs should not be taken for at least two weeks before starting this medication. Carefully review the labels of all your medications, including allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness or increase your heart rate or blood pressure. Caffeine can amplify the side effects of this medication. This drug may also interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests, such as brain scans for Parkinson's disease, potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Appetite suppressants should not replace a proper diet. Do not share this medication with others. Regular medical and laboratory tests, such as blood pressure monitoring, heart evaluations, and kidney function tests, should be conducted while taking this medication. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Phentermine is used as part of a doctor-approved program that includes exercise, behavioral changes, and a reduced-calorie diet to help with weight loss. It is prescribed for certain overweight individuals, such as those who are obese or have weight-related medical conditions. The exact mechanism by which this medication aids in weight loss is not fully understood, but it may work by suppressing appetite, increasing energy expenditure, or affecting specific areas of the brain. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, usually once daily, one hour before breakfast or one to two hours after breakfast. If necessary, your doctor may adjust your dose to a smaller amount taken up to three times daily. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. For sustained-release capsules, take the dose once daily before breakfast or at least 10 to 14 hours before bedtime. Swallow the capsules whole; do not crush or chew them. If using orally dissolving tablets, take them once daily in the morning, with or without food. Dry your hands before handling the tablet. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. Your doctor will adjust the dose to determine the most effective amount for you. Discuss the risks, benefits, and duration of phentermine treatment with your doctor. To achieve the best results, take this medication regularly, exactly as prescribed, and for the duration directed by your doctor. Abruptly stopping this medication may result in withdrawal symptoms, such as depression or severe fatigue. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose. Withdrawal is more likely if you have used phentermine for an extended period or in high doses. While this medication helps many individuals, it may sometimes lead to addiction. The risk of addiction is higher if you have a history of substance use disorder, such as overuse of or addiction to drugs or alcohol. Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. This medication may lose its effectiveness after a few weeks of use. If this occurs, consult your doctor. Do not increase the dose unless directed by your doctor. Common side effects include dizziness, dry mouth, difficulty sleeping, irritability, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. This medication may raise your blood pressure. Rarely, it can cause serious, sometimes fatal, lung or heart problems, such as pulmonary hypertension or heart valve issues. The risk increases with prolonged use or when combined with other appetite-suppressant drugs or herbal products. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or other sympathomimetic amines (e.g., pseudoephedrine, amphetamine, diethylpropion) or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. This drug may cause dizziness, blurred vision, or, in rare cases, drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly and share the results with your doctor. If using orally dissolving tablets, be aware that they may contain aspartame. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. It may also pass into breast milk and could have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this drug.
